title: Triviality of promise polymorphisms
summary: Given two $m$-ary predicates $P,Q$, an $n$-ary polymorphism is a tuple $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of functions such that $x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(n)} \in P$ implies $(f_1(y_1),\dots,f_m(y_m)) \in Q$, where $y_i = (x^{(1)}_i,\dots,x^{(m)}_i)$. This generalizes the usual definition in universal algebra, in which $P = Q$ and $f_1 = \cdots = f_m$. In earlier work, we studied when all polymorphisms of a single predicate are "trivial": either all depend on a single coordinate (common to all of them), or they constitute a "certificate" for the predicate.
